assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: original seasonal-food atlas editorial illustration. Make one square image in visibly hand-painted realistic watercolor: soft translucent washes, delicate warm paper grain and refined brush edges, clearly an illustration rather than a photograph. Scene: a natural warm-white tabletop, a shallow plain pale ivory ceramic bowl, gentle daylight from upper left and very soft shadows. Subject: a small modest quantity, about fourteen, of clean pale cream and milk-yellow edible wasp brood removed from their nest, the mixed immature stages commonly sold as hu feng yong in southwest China. Several plump legless larvae are naturally C-curved with subtle rounded body segments and a very small warm amber head; a few very pale early pupae are slightly straighter with small folded appendage contours closely appressed to the body. Show individual whole pieces, varied gentle orientations, clean and delicate, without filling the bowl into an overwhelming heap. The food group is generalized immature Vespidae brood, not identified to any specific wasp species and not a claim of a real Zhenkang photograph. This must NOT resemble large hard brown silkworm chrysalises, long bamboo caterpillars, rice grains, adult bees, adult wasps or winged insects. No spread legs, striped adult abdomens, adult eyes or adult wings. Composition: a complete bowl seen from an overhead three-quarter angle, occupying 65 to 75 percent of the image; at least 10 percent breathing room around all four edges. All brood remain entirely in frame and comfortably small at natural table scale; calm, tidy and appetizing instead of a magnified insect macro. Palette: warm white, ivory, creamy yellow and a few subdued pale amber details. No nest, no honeycomb, no insects walking outside bowl, no garnishes, no text, no labels, no watermark, no decorative patterns, no people, no tools, no blood, no discarded body parts, no black background.

assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: original ingredient/dish editorial illustration for a Chinese seasonal-food atlas. Create one square image, visibly hand-painted realistic watercolor with delicate paper grain and soft brush edges, clearly an illustration rather than a photograph. Scene: a natural warm-white tabletop, a shallow plain pale ivory ceramic plate, soft daylight from upper left, calm appetizing editorial mood. Subject: five small whole cooked aquatic dobsonfly-family larvae, the local Chinese food group called pa sha chong, presented neatly and separately on the plate with very sparse finely sliced green scallion. Use family-level generalized Corydalidae larval anatomy, do not imply identification to a particular species. Accurate recognizable form: flattened elongated bodies, about ten evident body sections, a small dark head with discreet short mandibles, three pairs of small articulated true legs clustered on the front thorax, paired slender lateral abdominal filaments along the middle and rear body, tapering rear with two short terminal appendages. These are NOT terrestrial centipedes: do not draw many identical walking legs along the full length. They are NOT bamboo worms, silkworm pupae, marine sandworms, shrimp, caterpillars, or adult winged insects. Cooked bodies are muted olive-brown and warm chestnut, lightly crisp with restrained sheen. Keep complete heads, bodies, lateral filaments, and tails visible, gentle natural curves, modest head size, no exaggerated fangs, no snarling or frightening monster anatomy. Composition: overhead three-quarter view with the complete plate and food group occupying about 70 percent of image, at least 10 percent clean breathing room on all four sides. No close-up macro scale, no crop, no dramatic dark shadows, no blood, no people, no tools, no discarded limbs, no text, no labels, no watermark, no decorative plate pattern.
